mechanism_narrative: Increasing GDP indicates strong economic activity, which should positively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If GDP growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in unemployment rate above 8% signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If UNRATE exceeds 8% but S&P 500 returns remain positive more than 35% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: When both industrial production and housing starts increase, it indicates strong economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If both proxies increase but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 30% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, higher federal funds rates negatively impact S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS increases but S&P 500 returns remain positive more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Growth in payroll employment suggests a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: If PAYEMS growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 45% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in real estate investment signals strong demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If RSAFS growth exceeds 5% but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 35% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: When inflation (CPIAUCSL) rises and unemployment (UNRATE) is high, it creates economic uncertainty, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If both CPIAUCSL and UNRATE are high but S&P 500 returns remain positive more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: During late-cycle expansion, GDP growth slows, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 growth is below 2% but S&P 500 returns are positive more than 35% of the time.
